verification_report.summary: All submitted statements and proofs pass sequential verification under the supplied internal premises and standard inputs. Local comparison uses the correct ordered-contact directions, the ordinary bounded envelope contact theorem, and cancellation only for locally finite measures. The strengthened strict barrier and the one-sided bound v<=u+C1 keep infimizing sequences away from the poles, validating global domination; constant shifts then give both order assertions. The reciprocal construction has nonnegative current coefficients summing to one, applies the Lp subsolution premise only to omega, extends across the analytic pole set, and preserves eta within the stated bounded difference with a uniform density bound. The Gauduchon estimate correctly uses the full linear current wedge and distributional Stokes, including any mass at the poles. Separate freezing of theta and gamma produces bounded ordinary psh functions satisfying [Dinew09, Theorem 1.2](https://arxiv.org/pdf/0705.0974); the smooth-volume density conversion and vanishing-error limit are valid. Normalized compactness and dominated convergence give uniform upper bounds for exponential suprema and the normalized positive constants. The [published BGL25 Section 4](https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s42543-025-00105-2) attribution matches the nonclosed big setting and explicitly drops BMP; its conclusions were not used as premises. The accepted local envelope input also matches [the published ordinary envelope contact theorem, Theorem 2.7](https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s00208-024-03003-7). No closedness, semipositivity of theta, BMP, PVP, or finite total top-degree mass was introduced. No general-measure existence conclusion is inferred. No critical errors or gaps were found.
